item.title: Ch1.2 RAG Overview
item.description:
In the previous section, we introduced in detail the background and motivation for the emergence of RAG, understood why RAG is needed, and what RAG can ultimately help us achieve. In this section, we will introduce the basic process of RAG development.

1. Core Motivation: Why is RAG needed?

First, let’s do a simple review.

The primary driving force behind RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) lies in the limitations of LLM pre-trained data. Despite the large scale of LLM pre-training, they cannot incorporate users’private dataorthe latest dataafter pre-training.

item.title: Ch1.1 What's RAG?
item.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) are trained on large but fixed corpora, which limits their ability to reason about private or up-to-date information. Fine-tuning is a way to mitigate this issue, but it is generally not suitable for recalling factual information and is relatively costly. Against this backdrop, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has gradually emerged as a mainstream and powerful mechanism. RAG uses documents retrieved from external data sources as a Knowledge Base to enhance the generation capabilities of LLMs through in-context learning.
